commit_message:
Bug 1992888 - Remove the data header from wasm GC inline array allocations.  r=rhunt,bvisness.

This patch reworks WasmArrayObject layout so as to remove the need for a
payload header word in inline allocations.  OOL payloads still need a header
word.  The scheme is:

* IL arrays have no header word.  Instead the payload begins *immediately*
  (with no alignment gap) after the data pointer field.  Because the payload
  array is constrained to be 8-aligned within the object, this means the data
  pointer will hold an 8-aligned value.

* OOL arrays have an 8-byte header, WasmArrayObject::OOLDataHeader header
  word.  Forwarding addresses are stored in OOLDataHeader::word.  In principle
  this can be any value so long as its least significant bit is not zero.
  Hence it is possible to distinguish an IL from OOL payload pointer by
  looking at the word that precedes the pointer; if its least significant bit
  is zero the payload is IL, else it's OOL.

In practice, the OOLDataHeader::word values are used to store forwarding
pointers for the BufferAlloc-managed OOL blocks during GC.  We manage the
reading/writing of the forwarding pointers ourselves, to set their lowest bit
to 1 when storing them, so as to mark the associated area as OOL (see
WasmArrayObject::obj_moved).

When OOL areas are initially created, their header word is set to
OOLDataHeader_Magic, which is suitably misaligned, and is not a valid pointer.

Hence it is possible to also tell whether an OOL area has ever been relocated,
since relocation will overwrite the initial OOLDataHeader_Magic value.

The patch tightens up, and documents, the WasmArrayObject layout.  This is
necessary in order to guarantee that (1) the IL data area has an offset that is
0 % 8, and (2) that the `data_` field is right at the end of the object.

Main changes:

* WasmArrayObject::obj_moved, WasmStructObject::obj_moved: changes to store
  the forwarding address of an OOL block in the old block's
  OOLDataHeader::word field.

* Instance::updateFrameForMovingGC: update array OOL pointers using the
  forwarding addresses stored by WasmArrayObject::obj_moved.

* class WasmArrayObject: rework; tighten up layout a lot; add static assertions
  accordingly; simplify methods relating to layout/offsets.

* terminology: change `storageBytes` to `arrayDataBytes`.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D273553

findings.title: Incorrect bitwise operator corrupts OOL forwarding pointer in WasmArrayObject::obj_moved()
findings.message: When a WasmArrayObject with out-of-line (OOL) array data is promoted/relocated during a nursery minor GC, obj_moved() is supposed to store a forwarding pointer to the new OOL block location in the old block's OOLDataHeader::word field, with bit 0 set to mark it as a valid forwarding pointer (this bit is the documented protocol used by isDataInline()/Instance::updateFrameForMovingGC() to distinguish OOL forwarding words from inline array data). The code instead computes `uintptr_t(oolHeaderNew) & 1`, a bitwise AND, rather than `uintptr_t(oolHeaderNew) | 1`, a bitwise OR. Because oolHeaderNew is always an aligned pointer (its low bits are zero), the AND expression evaluates to 0 for every invocation, discarding the entire forwarding pointer and producing a header word indistinguishable from an inline-array header word (whose bit 0 is also clear). Consequently, Instance::updateFrameForMovingGC(), which reads this word via WasmArrayObject::isDataInline() to decide whether a wasm-stack-cached ArrayDataPointer needs to be redirected to the array's new location, misclassifies the moved OOL data as inline. It takes the inline code path, computes a bogus WasmArrayObject* from the stale data pointer, finds (via MaybeForwarded) that the bogus pointer is unchanged, and therefore leaves the stack slot pointing at the old (now freed/reused) nursery memory. Wasm code that resumes execution after the GC then reads and potentially writes through this stale pointer, resulting in a use-after-free that is reachable from untrusted web content via WasmGC (array.new/array.get/array.set across a call that can trigger a minor GC).
findings.suggestion: Use bitwise OR instead of AND so the forwarding pointer's value is preserved while its low bit is forced to 1 (the documented OOL marker), e.g. add an assertion that the pointer is already aligned (bit 0 clear) before OR-ing in the marker bit, matching the eventual upstream fix.

ground_truth.root_cause: In the OOL-forwarding branch of WasmArrayObject::obj_moved(), the intended bitwise-OR operation (`uintptr_t(oolHeaderNew) | 1`) that sets bit 0 of the forwarding pointer while preserving the pointer's upper bits was mistakenly written as a bitwise-AND (`uintptr_t(oolHeaderNew) & 1`). Since OOL header pointers are always aligned (bit 0 naturally clear), the AND operation always yields 0, destroying the forwarding pointer entirely instead of merely setting its tag bit.
